IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p99/r10.claim: The condemned are dragged toward Hell by their forelocks and feet; the forelock phrase denotes the person who bears it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r4.claim: On the certain Day of Judgment people cannot flee; foreheads expose sinners, who are seized and thrown into Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r4.anchor: no evidence will be needed to convict a criminal as his forehead will bear witness to his sins. He will then be grabbed by his forehead and feet and flung into Hell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r3.claim: Seizing criminals by forelocks and feet depicts their being thrown into Hell like logs; the action is implied by the image rather than stated.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r3.anchor: just as logs of wood are thrown into raging fire, these people shall be thrown into Hell. Here they being thrown into Hell is not stated in words

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r7.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies sinners' distinguishing marks as blackened faces and blue eyes; the author also allows blindness, muteness, deafness, or other disfigurement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r7.anchor: وسيما المجرمين: سواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون، قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says sinners are seized by forelock and feet, trampled together like firewood, and cast into the fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يؤخذ بناصيته وقدميه فيوطأ، ويجمع كالحطب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says forelock and feet are joined behind the sinner's back with a chain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك: يجمع بينهما في سلسلة من وراء ظهره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r10.claim: Other accounts say angels alternately take sinners by the forelock or feet, or drag different people by one or the other; the passive grammar omits the agent and object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r10.anchor: وقيل: تسحبهم الملائكة، تارة تأخذ بالنواصي، وتارة بالأقدام

TABRISI:96:16-19/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:16-19/r1.claim: Dragging by the forelock humiliates and disgraces him, as in the verse about taking sinners by their forelocks and feet; alternatively, fire burns and blackens his face.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r1.anchor: ومعناه لنذلنه ونقيمنه مقام الأذلة ففي الأخذ بالناصية إهانة

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r6.claim: An objection to the intercession reading is that the next verse’s statement that criminals are recognized by their marks does not fit it; al-Rāzī has supplied the grammatical and interpretive reply above.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r6.anchor: ثالثها : قوله : { يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم } ( الرحمن : 41 ) لا يناسب ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r1.claim: “Criminals are recognized” explains the common reading that no one asks who sinned; al-Rāzī asks how it fits readings where no one asks about another’s sin or seeks pardon.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r1.anchor: اتصال الآيات بما قبلها على الوجه المشهور ، ظاهر لا خفاء فيه ، إذ قوله : { يعرف المجرمون } كالتفسير

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r2.claim: The sign may be brands on their foreheads, linked to the verse describing foreheads being branded in Hellfire.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r2.anchor: أحدها : كي على جباههم ، قال تعالى : { يوم يحمى عليها فى نار جهنم فتكوى بها جباههم }

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r3.claim: Another possible sign is blackness, as in verses describing faces turning black.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r3.anchor: ثانيها : سواد كما قال تعالى : { فأما الذين اسودت وجوههم } ( آل عمران : 106 ) وقال تعالى : { وجوههم مسودة }

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r4.claim: A third possible sign is dust and gloom.

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī explains sīmā as resembling ḍayzā in form, with an original form sawmā from the root of the word for a distinguishing mark.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#2/r5.anchor: السيما كالضيزى وأصله سومى من السومة

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r1.claim: The singular passive “is seized” despite plural criminals may be governed by “by the forelocks,” or may imply a plural verb, “they are seized by the forelocks.”
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r1.anchor: المسألة الثانية : ما وجه إفراد ( يؤخذ ) مع أن ( المجرمين ) جمع ، وهم المأخوذون ؟ نقول فيه

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r2.claim: Taking governs a direct object when the thing itself is the aim, but uses bāʾ when it is only the physical means to seize something else; Quranic examples illustrate both constructions.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r2.anchor: الأخذ يتعدى بنفسه كما بينت ، وبالباء أيضا كقوله تعالى : { لا تأخذ بلحيتى ولا برأسى }

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r3.claim: The shift from “they are recognized” to impersonal “is seized” distinguishes universal recognition from capture by particular agents; the wording also makes the humiliating manner of seizure the focus.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r3.anchor: أما بيان النكال فلأنه لما قال : { فيؤخذ بالنواصى } بين كيفية الأخذ وجعلها مقصود الكلام

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r4.claim: Ordinary people and angels who need a sign recognize criminals by it, whereas the record-keeping and stern angels know them without needing a mark.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r4.anchor: بل يمكن أن يقال قوله : { يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم } المراد يعرفهم الناس والملائكة الذين يحتاجون في معرفتهم إلى علامة

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r5.claim: The phrase need not contradict bāʾ marking an instrument: the forelock is the rhetorical focus, but is seized as a means to capture its owner, not for being a forelock in itself.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r5.anchor: لأنا نقول : لا تنافي بينهما فإن الأخذ بالنواصي مقصود الكلام والناصية ما أخذت لنفس كونها

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r6.claim: One account binds each person’s forelock and feet together, either from behind so the chest protrudes or from the front so the head rests on the knees; al-Rāzī finds this account clearer.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فيؤخذ بالنواصى والاقدام } فيه وجهان أحدهما : يجمع بين ناصيتهم وقدمهم ، وعلى هذا ففيه قولان

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r7.claim: Another account has them dragged: some by the forelock and others by the feet.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r7.anchor: الوجه الثاني : أنهم يسحبون سحبا فبعضهم يؤخذ بناصيته وبعضهم يجر برجله ، والأول أصح وأوضح

RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r8.claim: The passive “is seized” leaves the listener waiting for the manner of capture, making seizure by forelocks the main point; a completed “they are seized” would make that detail secondary, though the phrasing still conveys their humiliation.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105#3/r8.anchor: أما إذا قال : فيؤخذ ، فلا بد له من أمر يتعلق به فينتظر السامع وجود ذلك ، فإذا قال : { بالنواصى } يكون هذا هو المقصود

STUDYQURAN:55:41/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r1.claim: The opening phrase may be an adverbial clause modifying verse 39: they are not questioned because their marks already identify them.
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r1.anchor: can also be read as an adverbial clause modifying v. 39, meaning that they will not be asked about their sins

STUDYQURAN:55:41/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r2.claim: The guilty are contrasted with believers, whose signs include light on the body parts washed in ablution or the mark of prostration mentioned in 48:29.
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r2.anchor: the marks by which the believers will be known, such as the light that shines from the parts of their bodies they washed when performing ablutions (IK)

STUDYQURAN:55:41/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r3.speaker: IK, Q
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r3.claim: One interpretation is that the guilty are bent down and bound by their heads to their feet.
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r3.anchor: their heads will be bent down and bound to their feet (IK, Q)

STUDYQURAN:55:41/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that angels drag the guilty by the forelock or by the feet.
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r4.anchor: the angels will drag them by the forelock or by the feet (Q)

STUDYQURAN:55:41/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r5.claim: The Quran elsewhere says every crawling creature is held by God by its forelock, at 11:56.
STUDYQURAN:55:41/r5.anchor: there is no creature that crawls, but that He holds it by its forelock (11:56)

TAB-FULL:v22p231/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r1.claim: The angels identify criminals by God-given marks: blackened faces and blue eyes.
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} [الرحمن: 41] قال: «يعرفون باسوداد الوجوه، وزرقة العيون»

TAB-FULL:v22p231/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says criminals are recognized by black faces and blue eyes.
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} [الرحمن: 41] قال: «يعرفون باسوداد الوجوه، وزرقة العيون»

TAB-FULL:v22p231/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r3.claim: Qatāda likewise identifies the criminals’ signs as blue eyes and black faces.
TAB-FULL:v22p231/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} [الرحمن: 41] قال: «زرق العيون، سود الوجوه»

BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r1.claim: Sīmā and sīmiyāʾ, with kasra and either shortened or lengthened form, mean a sign or mark; the sentence resumes as an explanation for why they are not questioned.
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r1.anchor: السيما والسيماء بالكسر والقصر والمد العلامة والجملة استئناف يجري مجرى التعليل لعدم السؤال

BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r2.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r2.claim: One view says criminals are recognized by black faces and blue eyes.
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r2.anchor: قيل يعرفون بسواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون

BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r3.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r3.claim: Another view says criminals are known by the gloom and grief upon them, while the righteous are known by the opposite signs.
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r3.anchor: وقيل بما يعلوهم من الكآبة والحزن كما يعرف الصالحون بأضداد ذلك

BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r4.claim: Nawāṣī is the plural of nāṣiya, the front of the head; here it means the hair at the front of the head. The prepositional phrase is the passive subject.
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r4.anchor: النواصي جمع ناصية وهي مقدم الرأس والمراد هنا شعرها والجار والمجرور هو القائم مقام الفاعل

BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r5.claim: The author distinguishes أخذَه, where the person taken is the object, from أخذ به, where the object is something associated with that person; he illustrates the latter with Quranic and idiomatic examples.
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r5.anchor: يقال أخذه إذا كان المأخوذ مقصودا بالأخذ وونه قوله تعالى خذوا حذركم ونحوه وأخذ به

BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r6.claim: Angels seize criminals by the hair of their forelocks and feet, throwing them into the fire, dragging them face-first, or binding forelock and feet together in a chain behind their backs.
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r6.anchor: تأخذ الملائكة بنواصيهم أي بشعور مقدم رؤوسهم وأقدامهم فيقذفونهم في النار أو تسحبهم الملائكة إلى النار

BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#3/r7.claim: The refrain about God's blessings here refers to the admonitions and deterrents in the threat.

TABATABAI:55:41-43/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r3.claim: The sentence answers an implied question—if they are not asked their sins, what happens to them?—so it is set apart rather than coordinated with what precedes.
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r3.anchor: في مقام الجواب عن سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل

TABATABAI:55:41-43/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r4.claim: Their sīmā is the conspicuous sign on their faces.
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r4.anchor: والمراد بسيماهم علامتهم البارزة في وجوههم

TABATABAI:55:41-43/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r5.claim: Nawāṣī is the plural of nāṣiya, the hair at the front of the head; aqdām is the plural of foot.
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r5.anchor: والنواصي جمع ناصية وهي شعر مقدم الرأس

TABATABAI:55:41-43/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r6.claim: The prepositional phrase bi-l-nawāṣī functions as the passive subject of yuʾkhadhu.

TABATABAI:55:41-43/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r7.claim: Though no one is asked about sin, criminals are recognized by facial marks, seized by forelocks and feet, and cast into the Fire.
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r7.anchor: يعرف المجرمون بعلامتهم الظاهرة في وجوههم فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام من المجرمين فيلقون في النار

TABRISI:55:37-45/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:37-45/r13.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:55:37-45/r13.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada identify the criminals' marks as black faces and blue eyes.
TABRISI:55:37-45/r13.anchor: أي بعلامتهم وهي سواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون عن الحسن وقتادة.

TABRISI:55:37-45/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:37-45/r14.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:55:37-45/r14.claim: Another explanation takes the marks to be signs of disgrace.
TABRISI:55:37-45/r14.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة. وقيل: بإمارات الخزي

TABRISI:55:37-45/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:37-45/r15.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:55:37-45/r15.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say guards bind criminals' forelocks and feet together, drag them, and cast them into the Fire.
TABRISI:55:37-45/r15.anchor: فتأخذهم الزبانية فتجمع بين نواصيهم وأقدامهم بالغل ثم يسحبون في النار ويقذفون فيها عن الحسن وقتادة.

TABRISI:55:37-45/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:37-45/r16.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:55:37-45/r16.claim: Another account says the guards seize them by forelocks and feet and drive them toward the Fire.
TABRISI:55:37-45/r16.anchor: وقيل: تأخذهم الزبانية بنواصيهم وبأقدامهم فتسوقهم إلى النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r1.speaker: جماعة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r1.claim: A group of exegetes says criminals are recognized by black faces and blue eyes, citing 3:106 and 20:102.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r1.anchor: قال جماعة المفسرين: يعرف بسواد الوجوه وزرقة الأعين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the criminals as Abū Jahl, al-Aswad, al-Walīd, and al-Naḍr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس في تفسير المجرمين في هذه الآية: يريد أبا جهل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says angels seize them by the forelocks while they are on the bridge and hurl them into the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r3.anchor: قال الكلبي: تأخذهم الملائكة وهم على الصراط بنواصيهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r4.speaker: الأعمش عن رجل عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash reports from an unnamed man from Ibn ʿAbbās that they are seized by forelock and feet, broken like firewood, and thrown into an oven.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r4.anchor: وروى الأعمش عن رجل عن ابن عباس قال يؤخذ بناصيته وقدميه فيكسر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq says their feet are bound behind them to their forelocks before they are thrown into the Fire, intensifying punishment and humiliation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق نجعل الأقدام مضمومة إلى النواصي من خلف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r8.claim: The criminals are recognized by their marks: black faces and blue eyes.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r8.anchor: { يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم } بعلامتهم، وهي سواد الوجوه، وزرقة العيون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r9.claim: Their forelocks are joined to their feet, and they are thrown into the Fire; “nawāṣī” is the plural of “nāṣiya,” forehead hair.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r9.anchor: { فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام } تضم نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم، ويلقون في النار

QASHANI:55:41-43/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:41-43/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:41-43/r1.claim: The criminals are those dominated by bodily dispositions formed through acquired and entrenched vices; these traits show in their outward signs.
QASHANI:55:41-43/r1.anchor: الذين غلبت عليهم الهيئات الجرمانية باكتساب الرذائل ورسوخها

QASHANI:55:41-43/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:41-43/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:41-43/r2.claim: Being seized by the forelocks signifies punishment from above: confinement and captivity through compounded ignorance and entrenched false beliefs.
QASHANI:55:41-43/r2.anchor: فيعذبون من فوق ويحجبون ويحبسون مقيدين أسراء من جهة رذيلة الجهل المركب

QASHANI:55:41-43/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:41-43/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:41-43/r3.claim: Seizure by the feet signifies punishment from below, dragging them face-down to Hell for bodily dispositions and practical vices such as greed, stinginess, lust, and anger.
QASHANI:55:41-43/r3.anchor: أي: يعذبون من أسفل، ويجرون ويسحبون على وجوههم

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r56.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r56.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r56.claim: Criminals are recognized by their marks and seized by their forelocks and feet, idiomatically caught by the collar and tail.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r56.anchor: perçemleriyle ayaklarından tutulur daha Türkçesi yaka paça yakalanırlar.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r57.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r57.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r57.claim: The refrain may be spoken as criminals are seized, or their seizure may itself count as a favor to those who are not criminals.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r57.anchor: mücrimlerin bu suretle yakalanması mücrim olmayanlar için bir nimet olur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r1.claim: After the scene of the Resurrection, humans and jinn are not asked about sins, sinners are hauled to Hell and made to enter and leave its fire, then fall into boiling water without relief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r1.anchor: 37. âyetin ardından insanlara ve cinlere günahları hakkında soru sorulmayacağı, günahkârların yaka paça cehenneme atılacakları ve inkâr edip durdukları bu gerçeği iyice bellemeleri için cehennem ateşine sokulup çıkarılacakları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r3.claim: Their deeds are recorded, their tongues, hands, and feet testify, and sinners are recognized by their faces, so no declaration is needed to establish their condition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r3.anchor: herkes dünyada yapıp ettiklerinin tek tek kayda geçirilmiş olduğunu görecek, günahkârların dilleri, elleri ve ayakları bu konuda tanıklık edecek, ayrıca 41. âyette ifade edildiği gibi günahkârlar simalarından tanınacaktır

BURHAN:v1p291/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p291/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p291/r1.claim: Lexical exegesis identifies intended meanings from context, so a Qur'anic exegete needs knowledge of Arabic nouns, verbs, and particles.
BURHAN:v1p291/r1.anchor: وهو يتصيد المعانى من السياق لأن مدلولات الألفاظ خاصة

BURHAN:v1p291/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p291/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو ابن الصلاح
BURHAN:v1p291/r2.claim: Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ explains that أهل المعاني in tafsir books means authors of works on Qur'anic meanings, such as al-Zajjāj and earlier scholars.
BURHAN:v1p291/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو عمرو ابن الصلاح وحيث رأيت فى كتب التفسير قال أهل المعانى فالمراد به مصنفو الكتب فى معانى القرآن

BURHAN:v1p291/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p291/r3.speaker: الواحدي
BURHAN:v1p291/r3.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the leading أهل المعاني include al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj, and Ibn al-Anbārī.
BURHAN:v1p291/r3.anchor: وفي بعض كلام الواحدى أكثر أهل المعانى الفراء والزجاج وابن الأنبارى

BURHAN:v1p291/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p291/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p291/r4.claim: Particles are treated in grammar books, while nouns and verbs are learned from lexicons; the author lists major works and reports Ibn Sida's lexicon at one hundred volumes.
BURHAN:v1p291/r4.anchor: وأما الأسماء والأفعال فيؤخذ ذلك من كتب اللغة وأكثر الموضوعات فى علم اللغة كتاب ابن سيد

BURHAN:v1p291/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p291/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p291/r5.claim: For verb lexicons, the source names works by Ibn al-Qūṭiyya, Ibn Ṭarīf, al-Saraqusṭī, and Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ, whose work it calls among the most comprehensive.
BURHAN:v1p291/r5.anchor: ومن الموضوعات فى الأفعال كتاب ابن القوطية وكتاب ابن طريف وكتاب السرقسطى المنبوز بالحمار ومن أجمعها كتاب ابن القطاع

BURHAN:v1p291/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p291/r6.speaker: يحيى بن نضلة المدني
BURHAN:v1p291/r6.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Naḍla reports Mālik's warning that an Arabic-ignorant person who interprets the Qur'an should be made an example.
BURHAN:v1p291/r6.anchor: قال يحيى بن نضلة المدينى سمعت مالك بن أنس يقول لا أوتى برجل يفسر كتاب الله غير عالم بلغة العرب

BURHAN:v1p291/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p291/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BURHAN:v1p291/r7.claim: Mujāhid says that a believer in God and the Last Day may not speak about the Qur'an without knowing Arabic.
BURHAN:v1p291/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد لا يحل لأحد يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر أن يتكلم فى كتاب الله إذا لم يكن عالما بلغات العرب

BURHAN:v1p291/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p291/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p291/r8.claim: Through ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās says وَسَقَ means gathered or collected and advises seeking rare Arabic meanings in poetry, citing an otherwise unidentified line.
BURHAN:v1p291/r8.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال إذا سألتمونى عن غريب اللغة فالتمسوه فى الشعر فإن الشعر ديوان العرب

ITQAN:v2p305/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p305/r1.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v2p305/r1.claim: Al-Zarkashi says an exegete must know Arabic vocabulary and grammar to uncover meaning: particles are treated in grammar books, while nouns and verbs are taken from lexicons, including the listed major dictionaries and verb glossaries.
ITQAN:v2p305/r1.anchor: ويحتاج الكاشف عن ذلك إلى معرفة علم اللغة أسماء وأفعالا وحروفا فالحروف لقلتها تكلم النحاة على معانيها

ITQAN:v2p305/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p305/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p305/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti prioritizes sound reports from Ibn ʿAbbas and his students for rare Qur'anic words, especially Ibn Abi Talha's route, which al-Bukhari used and arranged by surah.
ITQAN:v2p305/r2.anchor: وأولى ما يرجع إليه في ذلك ما ثبت عن ابن عباس وأصحابه الآخذين عنه فإنه ورد عنهم ما يستوعب تفسير غريب القرآن

RUMMANI:v1p108/r10.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p108/r10.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p108/r10.claim: Identifying criminals by their marks and seizing them by forelocks and feet is the strongest portrayal of humiliation.

DAMGHANI:v1p372/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r7.claim: Aqdām can refer literally to feet: the believers’ feet at Badr, and the feet of the guilty seized with their forelocks and cast into Hell.
DAMGHANI:v1p372/r7.anchor: القدم هي الرجل بعينها قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p485/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p485/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p485/r1.claim: Qadam is the familiar foot, from the ankle below the leg to the toes; it can also be metaphorical by context.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p485/r1.anchor: القدم : العضو المعروف . وحده من مفصل الكعب تحت الساق إلى الأظفار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p485/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p485/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p485/r2.claim: Qadam can mean the bodily foot.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p439#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p439#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p439#2/r1.claim: Their sīmā are identifying marks, such as blackened faces and blue eyes.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p439#2/r1.anchor: {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} أي بعلامات فيهم، يقال (3) : سواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون ونحو ذلك.

MAJAZ:v2p245/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p245/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p245/r1.claim: Sīmāhum means their identifying marks or signs.
MAJAZ:v2p245/r1.anchor: «يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم» (41) علاماتهم فى الأصل أعلامهم..

NAHHAS:v4p312/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p312/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p312/r4.claim: Sīmā and sīmiyāʾ mean a distinguishing mark.

NAHHAS:v4p312/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p312/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p312/r5.claim: In the passive construction, the phrase bi-al-nawāṣī can occupy the nominative position of the passive subject, or that subject can be implicit.
NAHHAS:v4p312/r5.anchor: يكون بالنواصي في موضع رفع اسم ما لم يسم فاعله ويجوز أن يكون مضمرا

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r1.speaker: حماد بن أبي سليمان
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r1.claim: Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān reads بسيمائهم with a lengthened vowel.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r1.anchor: وقرأ حماد بن أبي سليمان " بسيمائهم " بالمد.

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r2.claim: The Shaykh says يؤخذ takes ب because it is construed with the sense of يسحب, to drag.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r2.anchor: قوله: { فيؤخذ بالنواصي } " يؤخذ " متعد، ومع ذلك تعدى بالباء؛ لأنه ضمن معنى يسحب، قاله الشيخ.

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r3.claim: The author objects that يسحب takes على, as in 54:48, so دفع is a better implied sense for the preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r3.anchor: وسحب إنما يعدى ب " على " قال تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r4.claim: Makki says أخذت الناصية and أخذت بالناصية are both used, but not taking an animal by its forelock; Arab usage equates أخذت الخطام and أخذت بالخطام.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r4.anchor: وقال مكي: " إنما يقال: أخذت الناصية وأخذت بالناصية. ولو قلت: أخذت الدابة بالناصية لم يجز.

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r5.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r5.claim: Makki rejects the estimate كل واحد بالنواصي because the verb cannot take two objects, one introduced by ب.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r5.anchor: وقد قيل: إن تقديره: فيؤخذ كل واحد بالنواصي، وليس بصواب، لأنه لا يتعدى إلى مفعولين

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r6.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r6.claim: Makki allows two objects when one is introduced by a preposition other than ب, as in أخذت ثوبا من زيد; with ب a second object works causally.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r6.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يتعدى إلى مفعولين أحدهما بحرف جر غير الباء نحو: أخذت ثوبا من زيد.

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r7.claim: The author counters that أخذت الثوب بدرهم also governs through ب without a causal meaning, qualifying Makki’s distinction.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r7.anchor: لأنك تقول: أخذت الثوب بدرهم، فقد تعدى بغير " من " أيضا بغير المعنى الذي ذكره.

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r8.speaker: البصريون
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r8.claim: Basrans say the article in النواصي والأقدام does not replace a pronoun; they estimate بالنواصي منهم.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r8.anchor: وأل في النواصي والأقدام ليست عوضا من ضمير عند البصريين فالتقدير: بالنواصي منهم

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r9.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r9.claim: Kufans take the definite article in النواصي والأقدام as a substitute for an omitted pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r9.anchor: وأل في النواصي والأقدام ليست عوضا من ضمير عند البصريين فالتقدير: بالنواصي منهم، وهي عند الكوفيين عوض

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r10.claim: A ناصية is the front of the head.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r10.anchor: والناصية: مقدم الرأس. وقد تقدم هذا مستوفى في هود.

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r11.speaker: عائشة
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r11.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha asks why people do not تنصون their dead; the author glosses it as extending the forelock.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r11.anchor:
وفي حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها:
" ما لكم لا تنصون ميتكم "
، أي: لا تمدون ناصيته.

SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r12.claim: النصي names good pasture; calling someone a people’s forelock may mean he is useful and good, or their leader like رأس.
SAMIN-DURR:55:41/r12.anchor: والنصي مرعى طيب. وقولهم: " فلان ناصية القوم " يحتمل أن يكون من هذا

ZAJJAJ:v5p100/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p100/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p100/r9.claim: Zajjāj juxtaposes no one being asked with the command to question people; criminals are recognized by black faces and blueness, supported by 55:41, 3:106, and 20:102.
ZAJJAJ:v5p100/r9.anchor: فإذا كان ذلك اليوم كانت سيما المجرمين سواد الوجه والزرقة

ZAJJAJ:v5p102/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p102/r1.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p102/r1.claim: One view says their feet are joined to their forelocks from behind and they are thrown into the Fire, intensifying their punishment and humiliation.
ZAJJAJ:v5p102/r1.anchor: قيل تجعل الأقدام مضمومة إلى النواصي من خلف ويلقون في النار. وذلك أشد لعذابهم

ASAD-NOTES:55:39#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:39#n20/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:39#n20/r1.claim: Seizing sinners by forelocks and feet signifies utter humiliation; ancient Arabs used having one's forelock in another's hand as an idiom for subjection.
ASAD-NOTES:55:39#n20/r1.anchor: When the ancient Arabs wanted to stress someone's subjection to another person, they would say, "His forelock is in the hand of so-and-so."

NASHR:v1p46/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p46/r1.speaker: عبد الوهاب بن السبكي الشافعي
NASHR:v1p46/r1.claim: Al-Subki holds that the seven readings selected by al-Shāṭibī and the three additional readings are mutawātir, certainly revealed to the Prophet, and denial is ignorance.
NASHR:v1p46/r1.anchor: متواتر معلوم باليقين لا يتطرق الظنون ولا الارتياب إلى شيء منه والله أعلم. كتبه عبد الوهاب بن السبكي الشافعي

NASHR:v1p46/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p46/r2.speaker: عبد الوهاب بن السبكي الشافعي
NASHR:v1p46/r2.claim: For al-Subki, tawātur is certain for every Muslim, including an ordinary person who cannot memorize a single Quranic letter, not only specialist reciters.
NASHR:v1p46/r2.anchor: بل هي متواترة عند كل مسلم يقول أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدا رسول الله

NASHR:v1p46/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p46/r3.speaker: إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن محمد القراب
NASHR:v1p46/r3.claim: Al-Qurab says restricting practice to seven readings lacks transmitted or Prophetic warrant; a later compiler's seven-reading book became famous and fostered the public misconception that no more were permitted.
NASHR:v1p46/r3.anchor: وقال الإمام الأستاذ إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن محمد القراب في أول كتابه الشافي: ثم التمسك بقراءة سبعة من القرآن دون غيرهم ليس فيه أثر ولا سنة

NASHR:v1p46/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p46/r4.speaker: إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن محمد القراب
NASHR:v1p46/r4.claim: Al-Qurab notes that other books record many transmissions and variants for the imams, with no claim that unlisted transmissions are forbidden; a seven-transmission limit would leave each reader only one narration, which nobody accepts.
NASHR:v1p46/r4.anchor: ولو كانت القراءة محصورة بسبع روايات لسبعة من القراء لوجب أن لا يؤخذ عن كل واحد منهم إلا رواية، وهذا لا قائل به

NASHR:v1p46/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p46/r5.speaker: إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن محمد القراب
NASHR:v1p46/r5.claim: Al-Qurab rejects construing the hadith that the Quran was revealed upon seven aḥruf as referring to seven readers born after the Successors: that would make the report useless until their later appearance.
NASHR:v1p46/r5.anchor: وينبغي أن لا يتوهم متوهم في قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف، أنه منصرف إلى قراءة سبعة من القراء الذين ولدوا بعد التابعين

NASHR:v2p49/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p49/r1.speaker: صاحب التجريد
NASHR:v2p49/r1.claim: The author says al-Azraq's route through the author of al-Tajrīd uniquely opens all verse-final forms except those with rāʾ, whether wāwī or yāʾī, against the other transmitters from him.
NASHR:v2p49/r1.anchor: وانفرد صاحب التجريد عن الأزرق بفتح جميع رءوس الآي ما لم يكن رائيا سواء كان واويا، أو يائيا

NASHR:v2p49/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p49/r2.speaker: أبو طاهر بن خلف وعبد الجبار الطرسوسي وأبو الفتح فارس بن أحمد وأبو القاسم خلف بن خاقان
NASHR:v2p49/r2.claim: These transmitters report intermediate imāla for al-Azraq in all non-final yāʾī forms, matching al-Dānī's Taysīr and other works.
NASHR:v2p49/r2.anchor: فروى عنه إمالة ذلك كله بين بين أبو طاهر بن خلف صاحب العنوان وعبد الجبار الطرسوسي صاحب المجتبى

NASHR:v2p49/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p49/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن طاهر بن غلبون وأبوه وأبو محمد مكي
NASHR:v2p49/r3.claim: Tahir ibn Ghalbun, his father, Makki, and other authorities report full opening for al-Azraq on those yāʾī forms.
NASHR:v2p49/r3.anchor: وروى عنه ذلك كله بالفتح أبو الحسن طاهر بن غلبون، وأبوه أبو الطيب، وأبو محمد مكي بن أبي طالب

NASHR:v2p49/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p49/r4.speaker: الداbني والشاطبي والصفراوي
NASHR:v2p49/r4.claim: Al-Dānī in al-Jāmiʿ, al-Shāṭibī, al-Ṣafrawī, and their followers allow both intermediate imāla and opening for al-Azraq; the author affirms both as sound.
NASHR:v2p49/r4.anchor: وأطلق الوجهين له في ذلك الداني في جامعه، وغيره، وأبو القاسم الشاطبي والصفراوي، ومن تبعهم، والوجهان صحيحان

NASHR:v2p49/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p49/r5.speaker: صاحب المبهج
NASHR:v2p49/r5.claim: The author says al-Mubhij uniquely assigns intermediate imāla on all the listed forms to Qālūn through every route, contrary to all others; the known report is only through Ismāʿīl al-Qāḍī.
NASHR:v2p49/r5.anchor: وانفرد صاحب المبهج بإمالة جميع ما تقدم عن قالون من جميع طرقه بين بين فخالف جميع الناس

NASHR:v2p49/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p49/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p49/r6.claim: Although the Taysīr's wording appears to give Warsh opening for hudaay, muḥyāy, and mathwāy, the author rejects that inference: al-Dānī's other books, especially al-Imāla, explicitly give intermediate imāla.
NASHR:v2p49/r6.anchor: وذلك أنه لما نص على إمالتها للكسائي من رواية الدوري عنه في الفصل المختص به وأضاف إليه رؤياك نص بعد ذلك

NASHR:v2p49/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p49/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p49/r7.claim: The author likewise rejects readings of al-ʿUnwān that imply opening for Warsh in marsāhā and al-sūʾā; the correct rule gives intermediate imāla.
NASHR:v2p49/r7.anchor: وكذلك ظاهر عبارة العنوان في هود يقتضي فتح مرساها لورش، وكذا السوءى في الروم والصواب إدخال ذلك في الضابط المتقدم

NASHR:v2p402/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p402/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p402/r1.claim: For Qunbul outside the Ibn Mujāhid and al-Zaynabī routes, the author takes one short reading, reported without objection by Ibn Shānabūdh, Abū Rabīʿa, Ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ, and others.
NASHR:v2p402/r1.anchor: فلا ريب في الأخذ له من طرقهم بالقصر وجها واحدا لروايتهم كذلك من غير إنكار

NASHR:v2p402/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p402/r2.speaker: الزينبي عن قنبل
NASHR:v2p402/r2.claim: Through al-Zaynabī from Qunbul, the long reading is the sole face, like the rest of the group.
NASHR:v2p402/r2.anchor: وإن أخذ بطريق الزينبي عنه فالمد كالجماعة وجها واحدا

NASHR:v2p402/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p402/r3.speaker: ابن مجاهد عن قنبل
NASHR:v2p402/r3.claim: On Ibn Mujāhid's route, Ṣāliḥ al-Muʾaddib, Bakkār, al-Muṭawwiʿ, al-Shanabūdhī and others report short; Abū al-Ḥasan al-Muʿaddil, Abū Ṭāhir, and al-Kattānī report long; where both are attested, both are taken.
NASHR:v2p402/r3.anchor: وإن أخذ بطريق ابن مجاهد فينظر فيمن روى القصر عنه كصالح المؤدب وبكار بن أحمد والمطوعي والشنبوذي

NASHR:v2p402/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p402/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p402/r4.claim: The author says short is better established through performance and long stronger in textual reports, so he adopts both on Ibn Mujāhid's route, combining the two kinds of evidence; denying Ibn Mujāhid took short contradicts transmission.
NASHR:v2p402/r4.anchor: ولا شك أن القصر أثبت وأصح عنه من طريق الأداء، والمد أقوى من طريق النص، وبهما آخذ من طريقه جمعا بين النص والأداء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p265#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p265#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p265#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the criminals are recognized by blackened faces and blue eyes.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p265#2/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم ﴾ قال يعرفون باسوداد الوجوه وزرق الأعين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r1.claim: The statement that criminals are recognized by their signs is a fresh sentence explaining why they are not questioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r1.anchor: استئناف يجري مجرى التعليل لانتفاء السؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r2.claim: One reading replaces the expected pronoun with the explicit word criminals to specify that the people concerned are the sinners among humans and jinn.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r2.anchor: قيل : من وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير للإشارة إلى أن المراد بعض من الإنس وبعض من الجن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says their signs are black faces and blue eyes.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r3.anchor: سيماهمعلى ما روي عن الحسن سواد الوجوه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r4.claim: Another view takes their signs to be the gloom and grief visible on them; other proposed signs include blindness, dumbness, and deafness.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r4.anchor: وقيل : ما يعلوهم من الكآبة والحزن وجوز أن تكون أموراأخر الكعمى والبكم والصمم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r6.claim: النواصي is the plural of ناصية, the front of the head; الأقدام means the familiar feet.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r7.claim: The bā is instrumental, as in taking an animal by its bridle, and the prepositional phrase is the passive subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r7.anchor: والباء للآلة مثلها في أخذت بخطام الدابة والجار والمجرور نائب الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the bā as marking the object and the verb as carrying the sense of a verb that governs it, such as being dragged by the forelock.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r8.anchor: وقالأأبو حيان : إن الباء للتعدية والفعل مضمن معنى ما يعدي بها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r9.claim: Al may replace the possessive pronoun under the Kufan analysis, while Basrans posit an omitted pronoun; the author says that dispute matters only when a resumptive pronoun is needed here.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r9.anchor: أل فيهما عوض عن الضمير على مذهب الموفيين والضمير محذوف على مذهب البصريين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r10.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says an angel joins a sinner’s forelock and feet in a chain behind his back, breaks his back, and throws him into the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r10.anchor: على ما روي عن الضحاك أن يجمع الملك بين ناصية أحدهم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r11.claim: One explanation has some angels dragging sinners by their forelocks and others dragging them by their feet.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r12.claim: Another view has angels alternately dragging people by forelocks or feet, treating the conjunction as distributive or; the author says this departs from the apparent sense.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r13.claim: The agent is left unstated because it is self-evident; another explanation says the omission signals God’s greatness.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r13.anchor: وإبهام الفاعل لأنه كالمتعين وقيل : للرمز إلى عظمته

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r14.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r14.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet swore Hell’s angels were created a thousand years before Hell and grow stronger daily before seizing their victims by forelocks and feet; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#4/r14.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن مردويه والضياء المقدسي في صفة النار عن أنس قال : سمعت رسول الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#2/r1.claim: Sinners are recognized by black faces and blue eyes; the author links this to 3:106.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#2/r1.anchor: {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} ، وهو سواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#2/r2.claim: Their feet are joined to their forelocks from behind, and they are thrown into the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#2/r2.anchor: {فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام} ، تجعل الأقدام مضمومة إلى النواصي من خلف ويلقون في النار،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#3/r1.claim: From the statement that all on earth perish through this passage are admonitions, restraints, and warnings; they are blessings because they deter sin, which is why each verse ends by asking which favors are denied.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#3/r1.anchor: وكل ما ذكر الله تعالى من قوله: "كل من عليها فان" إلى ههنا مواعظ وزواجر وتخويف. وكل ذلك نعمة من الله تعالى، لأنها تزجر عن المعاصي ولذلك ختم كل آية بقوله: {فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان}

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:41-46/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:41-46/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:41-46/r1.claim: The criminals are recognized by the gloom and sorrow visible upon them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:41-46/r1.anchor: وهو ما يعلوهم من الكآبة والحزن

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:41-46/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:41-46/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:41-46/r2.claim: They may be seized by forelocks and feet together, or seized by forelocks at one time and by feet at another.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:41-46/r2.anchor: مجموعا بينهما، وقيل يؤخذون { بالنواصي } تارة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r18.claim: Although the wording is general, the context specifies recognizing criminals, rather than questioning them about sins or other matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r18.anchor: الكلام عاما عرف انه خاص بتعرف المجرم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r19.claim: Their sins, once hidden, become legible in signs such as blue eyes, black faces, blindness, deafness, and walking on their faces.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r19.anchor: زرقة العيون وسواد الوجوه والعمى والصمم والمشي على الوجوه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r20.claim: The righteous are also recognized by luminous white faces, smiling, and signs such as the ghurra and taḥjīl.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r20.anchor: وكما يعرف المحسنون بسيماهم من بياض الوجوه وإشراقها وتبسمها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r21.claim: The forelocks are the fronts of the heads; passive wording makes the criminals’ seizure seem effortless, by any captor appointed for it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r21.anchor: إلى سهولة الأخذ من أي آخذ كان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r22.claim: Their forelocks and feet are joined, then they are dragged helplessly by whoever God appoints and cast into the Fire; this reverses their habit of joining what God separated and separating what He joined.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r22.anchor: ما أمر الله به أن يفرق

DURR-FULL:v7p703/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says criminals are recognized by black faces and blue eyes.
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه في قوله {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} قال: بسواد وجوههم وزرقة عيونهم

DURR-FULL:v7p703/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj likewise identifies the marks as black faces and blue eyes.
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه {يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} قال: بسواد الوجوه وزرقة العيون

DURR-FULL:v7p703/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the keepers seize a person by forelock and feet, gather him up, and break him like firewood in an oven.
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام} قال: تأخذ الزبانية بناصيته وقدميه

DURR-FULL:v7p703/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r6.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says an angel takes a person by the forelock, joins it to the feet, breaks his back, and throws him into the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه في قوله {فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام} قال: يأخذ الملك بناصية أحدهم فيقرنها إلى قدميه

DURR-FULL:v7p703/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r7.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says the forelock and feet are joined in a chain behind the person’s back.
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: يجمع بين ناصيته وقدميه في سلسلة من وراء ظهره

DURR-FULL:v7p703/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r8.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r8.claim: A man from Kinda reports Aisha’s account of the Prophet: at the bridge there is no intercession; believers cross safely, while hypocrites are hooked by feet and forelock and cast into Hell, falling for fifty years; he says their weight equals five pregnant camels.
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r8.anchor: عن رجل من كندة قال: قلت لعائشة رضي الله عنها: أسمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3325#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3325#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3325#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the guards seize sinners by forelock and feet, gather them, and crush them like firewood in an oven.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3325#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : فيؤخذ بالنواصي والاقدام قال : تاخذ الزبانية بناصيته وقدميه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p256/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p256/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p256/r1.claim: The passage moves from worldly life to the afterlife because the preceding signs of God's power imply that He alone deserves worship; it threatens the polytheists and the jinn who led them to idolatry with judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p256/r1.anchor: هذا تخلص من الاعتبار بأحوال الحياة العاجلة إلى التذكير بأحوال الآخرة والجزاء فيها انتقل إليه بمناسبة اشتمال ما سبق من دلائل سعة قدرة الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p256/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p256/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p256/r7.claim: In context, the threat means that God will turn to the affairs of humans and jinn in the afterlife, as the following verse describes criminals recognized by their marks; it addresses the unbelieving majority of both kinds at revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p256/r7.anchor: والمناسب لسياق الآية باعتبار السابق واللاحق ، أن تحمل على معنى الإقبال على أمور الثقلين في الآخرة ، لأن بعده يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the criminals' marks as black faces and blue eyes among unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r12.anchor: والسيما التي يعرف بها المجرمون هي سواد الوجوه وزرق العيون في الكفرة، قاله الحسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r13.claim: The marks could also be other kinds of disfigurement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون غير هذا من التشويهات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says each unbeliever is seized by forelock and feet, folded like firewood, and cast into the Fire.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r14.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: يؤخذ كل كافر بناصيته وقدميه فيطوى ويجمع كالحطب ويلقى كذلك في النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r15.speaker: النقاش والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r15.claim: Al-Naqqāsh reports, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk also says, that folding is over the back in a hunched posture.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r15.anchor: وقال النقاش: روي أن هذا الطي على ناحية الصلب قعسا وقاله الضحاك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r16.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r16.claim: Others say the person is folded over the face.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r16.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل على ناحية الوجه، قالوا فهذا معنى: فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r17.speaker: قوم في كتاب الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r17.claim: A view in al-Thaʿlabī's book says the unbelievers are dragged, some by their feet and some by their forelocks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r17.anchor: وقال قوم في كتاب الثعلبي: إنما يسحب الكفرة سحبا، فبعضهم يجر بقدميه، وبعضهم بناصيته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the criminals are recognized by black faces and blue eyes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r1.anchor: قال الحسن بسواد الوجوه وزرق الأعين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r2.claim: Muqātil says Hell’s keepers join forelocks to feet behind the criminals’ backs and push them face-first into the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن خزنة جهنم تجمع بين نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم من وراء ظهورهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r3.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r3.claim: A second account says they are seized by forelocks and feet and dragged to the Fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r3.anchor: والثاني يؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام فيسحبون إلى النار ذكره الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r4.speaker: علي بن الفضيل بن عياض
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṣāʾigh reports that ʿAlī ibn al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ fainted during dawn prayer when this verse was recited; afterward he said its warning had occupied him despite the following verse about houris.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118#2/r4.anchor: ومعنا علي بن الفضيل بن عياض فلما قرأ يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم خر علي مغشيا عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r5.claim: The third view fits the stage after criminals are ordered to the Fire: they are no longer asked about sins but driven and thrown into it, as 55:41 describes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r5.anchor: لا يسألون عن ذنوبهم، بل يقادون إليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r6.claim: The criminals are recognized by visible signs on them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r6.anchor: يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم} أي: بعلامات تظهر عليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say the signs are blackened faces and blue eyes; the author compares this recognition with believers’ ablution marks, the radiance and whiteness of their limbs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: يعرفونهم باسوداد الوجوه وزرقة العيون. قلت: وهذا كما يعرف المؤمنون بالغرة والتحجيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r1.claim: The wardens join a criminal’s forelock to his feet and throw him into the Fire that way.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام} أي: تجمع الزبانية ناصيته مع قدميه، ويلقونه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r2.claim: Al-Amash reports Ibn Abbas saying the criminal is seized by forelock and foot and broken like wood in an oven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r2.anchor: وقال الأعمش عن ابن عباس: يؤخذ بناصيته وقدمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the forelock and feet are joined in a chain behind the criminal’s back.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: يجمع بين ناصيته وقدميه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the unbeliever’s forelock is tied to his feet and his back twisted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: يجمع بين ناصية الكافر وقدميه، فتربط ناصيته بقدمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r5.claim: Aisha relates that the Prophet said he would not intercede at the placement of the bridge, the judgment of faces, or the bridge itself; it is sharpened like a sword and hot as an ember, believers cross unharmed, while a hypocrite falls and wardens hook him by forelock and feet into Hell, where he falls for fifty years.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r5.anchor: قال: أتيت عائشة فدخلت عليها، وبيني وبينها حجاب، فقلت: حدثك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r6.claim: The author calls the report very anomalous, notes objectionable wording attributed to the Prophet and an unnamed transmitter, and says it cannot serve as proof.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499#2/r6.anchor: وفيه ألفاظ منكر رفعها، وفي الإسناد من لم يسم، ومثله لا يحتج به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says the forelock and foot are joined in a chain behind the criminal's back.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك : يجمع بين ناصيته وقدمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r2.claim: Another view says angels drag criminals, alternately seizing them by forelocks and feet.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r8.claim: The blessing in describing this terror is rescue by God's mercy and grace; warning of it is itself a kindness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449#2/r8.anchor: ونعمة الله فيما ذكره من هول العذاب : نجاة الناجي

MUQATIL:55:41-42/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r1.claim: After judgment, criminals are recognized by black faces and blue eyes.
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r1.anchor: بعد الحساب يعني بسواد الوجوه وزرقة الأعين

MUQATIL:55:41-42/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r2.claim: Hell's keepers bind their hands to their necks, join forelocks to feet from behind, and drive them face-first into the Fire.
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r2.anchor: خزنة جهنم بعد الحساب يغلون أيديهم إلى إعناقهم، ثم يجمعون بين نواصيهم إلى أقدامهم من ظهورهم، ثم يدفعونهم في النار على وجوههم

MUQATIL:55:41-42/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r3.claim: As they approach the Fire, the keepers tell them this is the fire they denied in worldly life, echoing 52:14.
MUQATIL:55:41-42/r3.anchor: هذه النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#10/r1.claim: The sinners are recognized by black faces and blue eyes.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#10/r2.claim: They are seized at times by the forelocks and at times by the feet.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#10/r2.anchor: اى يؤخذ تارة بالنواصى وتارة بالاقدام

QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r1.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r1.claim: Hasan says the criminals' signs are blackened faces and blue eyes.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: سواد الوجه وزرقة الأعين

QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi links these signs to verses describing blue-eyed criminals and contrasting white and blackened faces.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r2.anchor: قال الله تعالى: ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا

QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r3.claim: Angels seize criminals by the hair at the front of the head and their feet, then cast them into the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r3.anchor: أي تأخذ الملائكة بنواصيهم أي بشعور مقدم رؤوسهم وأقدامهم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r4.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says a chain joins a person's forelock and feet behind their back.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك: يجمع بين ناصيته وقدميه في سلسلة

QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak also says their legs are joined to their forelock until their back breaks, then they are thrown into the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r5.anchor: وعنه: يؤخذ برجلي الرجل فيجمع بينهما وبين ناصيته

QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r6.claim: One view says this treatment intensifies punishment and disfigurement.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r6.anchor: وقيل: يفعل ذلك به ليكون أشد لعذابه وأكثر لتشويهه

QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r7.claim: Another view says angels drag them to Hell face-first by the forelock or head-first by the feet.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r7.anchor: وقيل: تسحبهم الملائكة إلى النار تارة تأخذ بناصيته

QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r16.claim: The terrifying description of resurrection and punishment deters sin and encourages obedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:41-44/r16.anchor: والنعمة فيما وصف من هول القيامة وعقاب المجرمين ما في ذلك من الزجر
